history.gap: The five chart plates are rhythmically identical (card, caption row, one-line body, repeat) so the section reads as a list rather than a designed spread; the caption row itself (number · bold small caps · dotted leader · grey link) is a stock editorial pattern executed at 11px with no scale contrast to the plates above it. At the bar, plates would vary in scale and grid position (a full-bleed pair, then a narrow inset with a wide margin note), captions would carry a real secondary type size, and the mono annotations on mobile ("EQUAL HIGHS", "TRENDLINE LIQUIDITY", "FVG") would be re-laid rather than left colliding with candles and fib labels.
history.motion: Restrained fade-and-rise reveals with a clipped vertical wipe on the chart plates; competent, consistent, but generic and never surprising.
history.verdict: A is a disciplined, tightly kerned dark-editorial system whose only crime is safeness: every hairline, leader and mono label sits where it should, and the SVG chart tracings with gold annotations are genuinely distinctive material. B has the more cinematic ambition and a beautiful first photograph, but it fails the basic craft gates of contrast, label collision, dead space and copy proofing, so A takes it clearly without reaching shortlist.
